transcript:
Header: Recorded on 2026-04-10 16:00 PDT | Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Saintbridge CTO), Priya Nair (Saintbridge Security Lead), Marcus Chen (Saintbridge DevOps)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone - thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. I'm Alex from Redwood, and with me is Samira our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Jordan: Good, thanks. Ready to dig in. We brought Priya and Marcus on the call to cover security and infra.
[00:12] Alex: Great, quick agenda: high level questions about your security posture, then Samira will go deeper on deployment options and controls, and we'll close with next steps. Sound good?
[00:21] Priya: Sounds good.
[00:23] Samira: Yep.

[00:30] Alex: To start, Jordan can you give a bit of context - what are you evaluating and timeline?
[00:35] Jordan: Sure. We're building a clinical documentation assistant that will touch PHI in some flows, so security and compliance are non-negotiable. We're looking at hosted vs dedicated vs private. Target is pilot in Q3, production H1 next year. Primary concerns are compliance evidence (SOC 2, ISO), SSO integrations, auditability, and key management.
[01:02] Alex: Understood. When you say PHI - is it all PHI, or a subset in certain environments?
[01:06] Jordan: A subset - some patient notes will be processed; others we plan to redact. For pilot we'll likely keep data within our VPC if possible.
[01:13] Priya: On compliance, we need SOC 2 Type II, and ISO 27001 evidence ideally. Also details on penetration testing cadence and third-party attestations.
[01:22] Alex: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ... we also have ISO 27001 certification, yes. I'll share the PDF reports after the call. We also do annual pen tests and have vendor attestation details.
[01:33] Priya: Okay, can you also share scope - hosted vs dedicated - what is in-scope for the compliance reports?
[01:38] Samira: Quick clarifier - for hosted API our control plane is Redwood-managed, and we can provide SOC 2 evidence for the hosted environment; for Dedicated we provide customer-dedicated GPU pools and we have documentation on the boundary and responsibilities. For Private deployments you get a customer-managed control plane - the compliance posture shifts because you're responsible for some of the controls. We'll include the shared responsibility matrix in the docs.

[02:10] Marcus: From infra side we need SSO/SAML with SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC to limit who can call models, and audit logs we can ship to our SIEM. How granular are your logs?
[02:24] Samira: We have token-level request logs, per-route/model latency and cost metrics; audit logs capture API calls, config changes, and user actions. For Dedicated we emit more detailed logs and support exporting to syslog/CloudWatch/Stackdriver. We can also stream audit logs to your S3 or to our enterprise log collector.
[02:42] Marcus: And are logs immutable? We need tamper-evidence for some workflows.
[02:47] Samira: We can provide append-only log delivery and recommend MTLS + signed delivery to your collector. For Private deployments you'd control the storage and can lock down access with IAM policies.

[03:05] Priya: Encryption - do you support customer-managed KMS? We need CMEK for keys and separation.
[03:10] Alex: Yes, we support customer-managed keys in our Dedicated and Private offerings. For Hosted we support CMEK where the customer provides an external KMS integration (cloud KMS). We can show the KMS integration guide.
[03:21] Priya: Is end-to-end encryption for in-transit and at-rest default?
[03:25] Samira: TLS1.2/1.3 in transit, at-rest AES-256 by default. For Private we can support HSM integrations for additional key protection.

[03:40] Jordan: Data residency - we need data to stay in EU for certain customers. How does Redwood handle region pinning and data residency controls?
[03:47] Alex: We support region routing and data residency for Hosted, and Dedicated deployments can be provisioned in a specific region. For Private, obviously you control the region. We'll need to map exact flows - logs, backups, KV caches - to make sure nothing leaves the region.

[04:05] Marcus: About model caching - is any customer data persisted in caches that could be shared?
[04:10] Samira: We use per-customer KV caches and prefix caching; caching is isolated per customer/tenant. For high-security customers we offer cache bypass and strict TTLs. We'll include details in the security design doc.

[04:28] Priya: RBAC - can you scope roles and fine-grained permissions? We don't want engineers accidentally switching models in prod.
[04:34] Samira: Yes, role-based access and scoped API keys are standard. You can create routes with permissions and assign roles via SSO/SCIM. There's also a policy layer for canary rollouts and model pinning so only specific roles can change model versions.

[04:53] Jordan: For the hosted API - what is the shared responsibility matrix? If something goes wrong, what's Redwood responsible for vs us?
[04:59] Alex: We'll share a one-pager. High level: Redwood manages runtime, infra, patching for hosted; customer responsible for data classification, client-side encryption if used, and prompt-level redaction. For Dedicated we manage the cluster but some network controls are shared; Private you're mostly responsible for infra hardening.

[05:20] Priya: Audit logs retention policy - do you retain logs for 12 months? 24 months?
[05:25] Samira: Default retention is 90 days for detailed logs, 1 year for aggregated metrics. For enterprise we can extend retention to 2+ years and export to your storage for longer retention.

[05:40] Marcus: Pen tests - do you provide report summaries and remediation timelines?
[05:45] Alex: We can share pen test summaries and SOC 2 pen test references. For enterprise customers we can coordinate remediation with our security team and provide timelines.

[06:00] Priya: On SSO - we need SAML 2.0 + SCIM for provisioning and SCIM deprovisioning. Can you automate role mapping?
[06:08] Samira: Yes SAML 2.0 supported, SCIM v2 for provisioning, and role mappings can be configured from IdP groups to Redwood roles. We'll send a configuration guide with example metadata and claim mappings.

[06:28] Jordan: Does Redwood do data deletion on request? Our retention policy requires deletion within 30 days on customer request.
[06:34] Alex: We support data deletion APIs and can provide proof-of-deletion. For Hosted we delete request logs and cached artifacts per policy; for Dedicated/Private you can enforce deletion yourself. We'll add details to the data handling section.

[06:53] Priya: For legal and procurement, we'll need DPA language and any subprocessor lists.
[06:59] Alex: We'll include DPA and subprocessor list in the packet.

[07:05] Marcus: A technical question - latency-sensitive inference: can you guarantee latency SLOs for dedicated pools and what monitoring do you expose?
[07:13] Samira: Dedicated has SLO-backed profiles; we expose per-token latency histograms, p99s, and tracing hooks. For strict latency we recommend reserved pools + autoscale policies. We'll propose some default configs in the follow-up docs.

[07:36] Jordan: Any red flags if we start with Hosted for pilot and move to Dedicated for production?
[07:41] Alex: No, that's a common path. We'll document the migration steps and model version pinning. Migration mostly requires updating routing and re-validating KMS/KV cache configs.

[07:55] Priya: Regarding incident response - do you share post-mortems and notify customers on incidents that affect availability or security?
[08:03] Alex: Yes, we have an incident response policy and notify in-scope customers based on severity. We'll share our IR playbook high-level.

[08:15] Samira: Quick note on private deployment: Some customers prefer air-gapped packages with our control plane thin client. In those cases, the security responsibility is largely on the customer, but we provide the install bundle and ops runbook.

[08:33] Marcus: For logging export, can we get a sample CloudWatch / Splunk JSON schema?
[08:38] Samira: Yes, we'll include sample schemas and a CloudFormation example.

[08:45] Priya: Anything else we should be thinking about from security perspective?
[08:49] Jordan: I think we've covered the main items. Priya, Marcus - anything to add?
[08:53] Priya: Please include a clear breakdown of what is covered in SOC2 for Hosted vs Dedicated.
[08:58] Marcus: And performance benchmarking on Dedicated for our token rates - we'll want to run a benchmark.

[09:06] Alex: Great - recap next steps: We'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, DPA and subprocessor list, KMS guide, SAML/SCIM config guide, and schedule a technical deep dive. Samira will reach out to book that.

[09:24] Jordan: Thanks, appreciate it.
[09:26] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email.

End of transcript.
